text:
Erik Karlsson is 36, a three-time Norris winner, and suddenly the hottest name in the trade rumor columns. With Pittsburgh struggling, Pierre LeBrun reported this week that Carolina is interested, and the speculation hasn't stopped since. Nothing has happened yet, and the Penguins keep playing him nearly 24 minutes a night, more than 24 and a half over his last ten games.

The points look like Karlsson: 19 in 19 games, 16 of them assists, 10 on the power play. His finishing is right where it should be, 3 goals on 3.2 expected, and our talent range thinks his scoring pace is only a little ahead of itself.

Five on five is the problem. Pittsburgh gets 47% of the expected goals with him on, and its share is more than nine points worse than when he sits. That's a big gap for a player Evolving-Hockey had in the 91st percentile among defensemen for driving play last season, against the toughest competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still had him among the league's best passing defensemen. For a contender, the question is which Karlsson they'd be getting: the one on the power play, or the one on this five-on-five line.
headline: Karlsson, the biggest name on a struggling team
